**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً ۖ قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا ۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ﴾
Remember, O Children of Israel, the wrongdoing of your forefathers, and how stubborn they were and how much they argued with Musa, peace and blessings be upon him, when he said to them: "Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." They said, arrogantly: "Are you making us a target of mockery and ridicule?" Musa answered them: "I seek refuge with Allah from being one of those who mock."

﴿فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ﴾
They said: "Ask your Lord to make clear to us what this cow is like." He answered them: "Allah says to you that it is neither old and worn out, nor young and immature, but in between the two. So hurry to carry out your Lord's command."

﴿قَالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ ۚ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾
… They said: "Now you have brought the true description of the cow." So they were forced to slaughter it after a long time of evasion, and they almost did not do it because of their stubbornness. And so they were hard on themselves, and Allah was hard on them.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Allah command the Children of Israel to do? And if they had slaughtered any cow the first time, what would have happened?
2. Every time they asked a new question, what happened to them?
3. Does this mean that asking questions is bad? (No; asking in order to understand and learn is praiseworthy. What is blameworthy is asking out of stubbornness, to escape the work and delay it.)

**This week's exercise**
This week, when your child is asked to do something clear, like tidying their room or making wudu for the prayer, they hurry to do it the first time without arguing, and you both put a mark on a sheet of paper every time they do. At the end of the week, talk together about the time and the quarrels that hurrying saved.
